deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Grothendieck's account of the Monsky–Washnitzer idea, written for his 1966–67 crystalline lectures. The problem: given a smooth affine X_0 over a perfect field k of characteristic p, lift it to a smooth formal scheme 𝔛 over S = Spf W(k). Such a lift exists by SGA 1 III and is unique up to non-unique isomorphism. The naive candidate cohomology is the de Rham cohomology of the completed lift, H^*(Γ(𝔛, Ω^•_{𝔛/S})). Grothendieck checks that this is far too large, using the affine line.

Take X_0 = Spec k[t]. Then 𝔛 = Spf W{t}, where W{t} is the ring of restricted power series Σ a_n t^n with a_n → 0 p-adically. The first de Rham cohomology is
H^1 = Ω^1/dO ≅ W{t}/Im(f ↦ f').

A restricted series Σ a_n t^n dt is exact exactly when its formal antiderivative Σ a_n t^{n+1}/(n+1) is again restricted. Rationally this means v_p(a_n) − v_p(n+1) → +∞, or multiplicatively |a_n|_p / |n+1|_p → 0, i.e. |a_n|_p = ε_n |n+1|_p with ε_n → 0.

Because v_p(n+1) takes arbitrarily large values, the condition v_p(a_n) → ∞ (restrictedness) does not suffice. So H^1 is huge: even modulo torsion it has infinite rank over W, whereas the right answer for the affine line is 0. Integration does not preserve convergence on the closed unit disc.

The next page draws the consequence. Monsky–Washnitzer replace the arithmetically awkward exactness condition by overconvergence, |a_n| = O(ρ^{-n}) for some ρ > 1, giving the weakly complete algebras W^†{t_1,…,t_n} and their quotients. This is the standard motivation for dagger algebras and for Monsky–Washnitzer and, later, rigid cohomology.
errors: Minor imprecision about integrality. Over W itself, exactness also requires a_n/(n+1) ∈ W for every n, i.e. v_p(a_n) ≥ v_p(n+1) for all n, not just the limit condition. The stated condition v_p(a_n) − v_p(n+1) → ∞ is exact only after tensoring with Q. Grothendieck implicitly signals this with 'sauf en torsion', so it is not a real error.

Not an error but worth noting: the image of d contains all polynomials, which are dense in W{t}. The quotient H^1 is therefore not even separated for the p-adic topology, a further pathology not mentioned on the page.

ideas.what: De Rham cohomology of the p-adically completed (restricted power series) lift of a smooth affine variety is too big; for the affine line, H^1 = W{t}/d(W{t}) has infinite rank modulo torsion.
ideas.modern_name: Failure of de Rham cohomology of the formal (p-adic completion) lift; motivation for overconvergence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Monsky–Washnitzer (Formal cohomology I, Annals 1968; announced c.1965–66)
ideas.where_published: Possibly mentioned in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968), which discusses Monsky–Washnitzer; unsure whether this explicit example is there.

ideas.what: Explicit criterion for a restricted series to be a derivative in W{t}: |a_n|_p/|n+1|_p → 0.
ideas.modern_name: Exactness criterion for 1-forms on the closed unit disc; loss of convergence under integration

ideas.what: Replacement by overconvergent series |a_n| = O(ρ^{-n}), ρ > 1 (next page), whose de Rham cohomology is correct.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard exposition of the well-known Monsky–Washnitzer motivating example (the affine line has huge de Rham H^1 over restricted power series). It is correct and pedagogical, with nothing new relative to the literature.

'et comme v_p(n) prend (pour n variable)': the bracketed [?] is 'n'.
'En notations multiplicatives, si | |_p est la valeur absolue p-adique, on veut que' (struck word before 'on veut').
